vulnerabilities.description: Project IDs and MCP server names hardcoded in installation commands. These should be environment variables.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Use environment variables or config files for sensitive configuration

vulnerabilities.description: Template paths constructed without validation. Could allow reading arbitrary files via '../' sequences.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Validate profile parameter against whitelist before path construction. Use path.normalize() and check against base directory.

vulnerabilities.description: User input in restArgs passed directly to execSync without proper escaping.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Use array-based child_process calls instead of string interpolation. Use 'shell' option carefully.

vulnerabilities.description: Server name validation only checks if config exists, doesn't validate against injection patterns.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Implement whitelist validation for server names. Use /^[a-z0-9-]+$/ pattern.

vulnerabilities.description: Environment variables resolved without sanitization. Could allow variable injection.
vulnerabilities.code: resolveEnvironmentVariable(obj) where values use process.env directly
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Validate and sanitize environment variable values before use

vulnerabilities.description: Memory file created without explicit permission settings. Default may be too permissive.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Explicitly set file mode to 0600: fs.writeFileSync(path, data, { mode: 0o600 })

vulnerabilities.description: Hook commands built with string interpolation, potential shell injection via description parameter.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Use execFile with arguments array instead of execSync with string templates

vulnerabilities.description: Files read without locking mechanism. Concurrent access could cause inconsistent reads.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Use fs.promises and consider file locking for concurrent access scenarios

vulnerabilities.type: Missing Error Handling in Child Process
vulnerabilities.description: spawn() call in createStdioConnection lacks error event handler for process failures.
Template variables replaced without escaping. Could allow code injection via malicious context values.
vulnerabilities.code: flatContext[key] values directly interpolated into content
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Escape special characters or use safer templating library (e.g., Handlebars with escaping)

recommendations: 1. IMMEDIATE: Implement input validation whitelist for all user-controlled parameters
2. IMMEDIATE: Replace all execSync with array-based child_process calls
3. HIGH: Move all hardcoded IDs and secrets to environment variables or .env files
4. HIGH: Implement proper path validation to prevent traversal attacks
5. HIGH: Add comprehensive error handling for all child process spawning
6. MEDIUM: Set explicit file permissions (0600) for sensitive files
7. MEDIUM: Use safer templating approach with automatic escaping
8. MEDIUM: Implement input validation patterns for all command/server names
9. MEDIUM: Add sanitization for environment variables before use
10. LOW: Implement file locking for concurrent database access
affectedModules: bootstrap-agent (HIGH RISK - path traversal, template injection)
